Artwork.description: The artwork object represents a product at a given media size and provides preview images for each page capable of hosting artwork imagery.

artwork.description: A list of URLs for preview images of each page in the artwork document, without customisations. Any pages without artwork will return `null`.

createdAt.description: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:ii:ss+00:00` formatted string to denote when this piece of artwork was created.

description.description: A longer description of the artwork.
description.example: Testing adding a 4p card via API call.

fullPath.description: The full SEO path to this artwork, which can be used as an alternate identifier when placing orders, generating previews etc.

id.description: Unique identifier for this piece of artwork. To be passed through to `Place Order` and similar calls requiring artwork IDs.

media.description: The media size associated with this piece of artwork.

name.description: The title of this piece of artwork.

revision.description: The revision number of this piece of artwork. Revision increases when artwork descriptors or image assets change.

slug.description: A search-engine-friendly identifier for this artwork. Can be added to your organisation domain to provide a path to the artwork's page, ie `/test-organisation/artwork-slug`.

updatedAt.description: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:ii:ss+00:00` formatted string to denote when this piece of artwork was last updated.

Artwork.title: Artwork Object

Contact.description: The contact object provides detail on a given record within a contact list. This contains their addressing information, unique identifiers (email, external ID where supplied) and any additional custom field data you may have supplied for the list.

address2.description: A secondary address line, typically containing a unit, apartment, suite number etc.

adminAreaLevel1.description: The state or province for this contact.

company.description: The company a contact belongs to, if supplied.

contactListId.description: Identifier for the contact list this contact belongs to.

country.description: A 2-character ISO code identifying the contact's country.

email.description: An email address for this contact, if supplied, which can be used to uniquely identify this contact for subsequent actions.

externalId.description: Any external identifier you have supplied for this contact which can be used to update this contact in future calls.

fields.description: Additional custom fields based on field codes for extended data on this contact record.

firstName.description: The first name of a contact.

fullName.description: The contact's full name, a combination of firstName & lastName.

lastName.description: The last name of a contact, if supplied.

latitude.description: Geo coordinates for this address, if it has been resolved with address lookups.

locality.description: A suburb or city for the contact.

longitude.description: Geo coordinates for this address, if it has been resolved with address lookups.

postcode.description: A postal code or ZIP code for this contact, where required by local addressing formats.

rawAddress.description: If a full, raw address was supplied for this contact, the original address as supplied by spreadsheet upload or application.
rawAddress.example: 1 Main Street, Brooklyn, New York, USA

requiresAction.description: If this contact was subject to address validation, whether this record requires manual intervention to resolve.

Contact.title: Contact Object

ContactList.description: The contact list object provides detail on a given list on your account, along with currently set up custom fields and automation details.

automations.description: The number of automation rules (active or disabled) currently applied to this list.

contacts.description: The number of unique contacts currently in this list.

description.description: An extended description on what this list is for or related notes, if required.

fields.description: List of `ContactListField` items that define additional information to store for each contact in the list.

id.description: Unique identifier for this contact list.

name.description: The human-readable name for this list.

rules.description: List of `ContactListRule` items that define rules to automatically send cards at specified intervals or based on triggers set up in the Cardly platform.

status.description: The current status of this contact list.

validation.description: High-level stats around the number of contacts pending / completed validation or requiring manual intervention.

pending.description: The total number of contacts pending address validation.

requireAction.description: The total number of contacts requiring manual review of their address data.

validated.description: The total number of contacts that have completed address validation.

ContactList.title: Contact List Object

ContactListField.description: The contact list field object defines additional, custom fields to be applied to all contacts within a list.

code.description: A human-readable code for this field, based on the field name. These don't change and can be used to reference additional data when syncing contacts.

description.description: Extended information about this field, if required.

id.description: A unique identifier for this field which never changes.

name.description: A human-readable label for this field.

status.description: The status of this field - currently always `active`.

type.description: The type of field this is, currently one of `text`, `date` or `number`.

ContactListField.title: Contact List Field

ContactListRule.description: A contact list rule object describes tasks be performed automatically at specified intervals or based on triggers set up in the Cardly platform.

annual.description: If true and linked to a `date` field, this automation will trigger yearly (ie, for birthday or anniversary type events).

bindings.description: Key-value mapped object of template variable code to contact list field for injecting data into the final card template.

format.description: Additional formatting to apply to the bound value, such as a number of years difference to the target send date.

name.description: The custom field ID or contact field name to map this template variable to.

cardArt.description: A list of `Artwork` entries to use for sends.

description.description: Extended information on this rule, if required.

enabled.description: Whether or not this automation is currently enabled for sending.

fieldId.description: The field ID linked to this validation rule as a trigger.

id.description: A unique identifier for this rule which never changes.

name.description: A human-readable name for this automation rule.

operator.description: The type of comparison (eq, db, da, etc) to apply to the trigger field.

templateId.description: The template to use for this rule.

value.description: The value to compare to in order to evaluate whether the trigger has succeeded or not.

ContactListRule.title: Contact List Rule

CreditHistory.description: The credit history object models an entry - positive or negative - for the organisation's credit purchase and spends.

change.description: Value that was either credited or debited from the organisation in this action.

effectiveTime.description: Timestamp of when this credit history entry occurred.

id.description: Unique identifier for this credit history entry.

newBalance.description: The current account credit balance at the time this change was effected.

notes.description: An extended description of what effected this balance change.

orderId.description: Identifier for an order that triggered this credit history entry. Generally used whenever paid transactions take place.

transactionId.description: Identifier for a transaction that triggered this credit history entry, typically related to the purchase of credits.

type.description: A human-readable, brief description of what this entry is for, ie; `Credit Purchase`, `Order Placement`.

typeCode.description: A short code to denote the type of change this was.

CreditHistory.title: Credit History Object

Doodle.description: The doodle object represents a vector-based image which can be included within card artwork.

description.description: An optional description of this doodle.

dimensions.description: Dimensions of this product in millimeters, exclusive of bleed.

height.description: Natural height of this doodle, in pixels.

width.description: Natural width of this doodle, in pixels.

image.description: A URL to a preview image of this doodle.

name.description: The human-readable name for this doodle.

restricted.description: Whether or not this doodle is exclusive to your organisation, or freely available across the Cardly platform.

slug.description: A human-readable identifier for this doodle.

Doodle.title: Doodle Object

Font.description: The font object models a style of writing available within Cardly, either from our shared library or your exclusive handwriting conversions.

canHumanise.description: Whether or not this font is marked for being eligible for humanisation techniques. Typically, screen or machine-readable fonts have this flagged off.

category.description: The category of writing this font falls into, one of `cursive`, `hand`, `serif`, `sans` or  `mono`.

familyVariants.description: The number of font variants this family contains for each character.

id.description: Unique identifier for this font option.

name.description: A localised, human-readable name for this font.

restricted.description: Whether or not this font is exclusive to your organisation, or freely available across the Cardly platform.

Font.title: Font Object

GiftCreditHistory.description: The gift credit history object models an entry - positive or negative - for the organisation's gift credit purchase and spends.

change.description: Value that was either credited or debited from the organisation in this action.

changeNet.description: Value that was either credited or debited from the organisation in this action, exclusive of tax.

changeTax.description:
Tax component for this transaction, were relevant. 

**Note:** currently, no region involves taxed gift card payments.

effectiveTime.description: Timestamp of when this gift credit history entry occurred.

id.description: Unique identifier for this gift credit history entry.

newBalance.description: The current account gift credit balance at the time this change was effected.

notes.description: An extended description of what effected this balance change.

orderId.description: Identifier for an order that triggered this gift credit history entry. Generally used whenever paid transactions take place.

transactionId.description: Identifier for a transaction that triggered this gift credit history entry, typically related to the purchase of credit.

type.description: A human-readable, brief description of what this entry is for, ie; `Credit Purchase`, `Order Placement`.

typeCode.description: A short code to denote the type of change this was.

GiftCreditHistory.title: Gift Credit History Object

Invitation.description: The invitation object provides detail on user that's been invited to your account and the status of that invitation.

accepted.description: When the invitation was accepted, if at all.

firstName.description: The invited user's first name, if known.

inviteSent.description: When the user's email invitation was sent.

lastName.description: The invited user's last name, if known.

accept.description: The acceptance URL for this invitation.

permissions.description: Permission-keyed list of permissions available once this invitation is accepted.

status.description: The current status of this invitation.

Invitation.title: Invitation Object

Media.description: The media object models a product available on Cardly and denotes the regions it is available for purchase in. It also provides information on the dimensions of the product, both physical and pixel dimensions for artwork supply.

height.description: Height of the artwork required for this product, in pixels, inclusive of bleed zones.

innerHeight.description: Height of the artwork inner area for this product, in pixels, exclusive of bleed zones.

innerWidth.description: Width of the artwork inner area for this product, in pixels, exclusive of bleed zones.

width.description: Width of the artwork required for this product, in pixels, inclusive of bleed zones.

bleed.description:
DimensionsBleed zone of this product in millimeters, added to the `dimensions` measurements for the overall page size.
Using the provided example, this would be a 115x158mm product for the purposes of artwork dimensions.

x.description: Left and right bleed zone measurements, in millimeters.

y.description: Top and bottom bleed zone measurements, in millimeters.

creditCost.description: The number of credits that would be consumed when ordering this media type.

description.description: A longer description of the product, along with any restrictions or important information.

dimensions.description: Dimensions of this product in millimeters, exclusive of bleed.

height.description: Height of this product, in millimeters, exclusive of bleed.

width.description: Width of this product, in millimeters, exclusive of bleed.

id.description: Unique identifier for this piece of artwork. To be passed through to `Place Order` and similar calls requiring artwork IDs.

name.description: A localised, human-readable name for this product.

pages.description: The total number of pages to this product. A standard greeting card is four pages (front, inner left, inner right, back), while a postcard-style product is two pages (front & back).

Media.title: Media Object

Order.description: The order object provides detail on a given order on your account, along with individual line item recipient, sender, cost and timing information.

costs.description: Contains details of the overall order costs.

customer.description: Details about the organisation or user that placed this order. For API-originating orders, this will be your organisation details.

items.description: List of `OrderItem` records that comprise this order.

origin.description: Where the order originated - via the API, your organisation portal, etc.

status.description: The current status of this order.

timings.description: Contains details of the overall order creation, update and payment times.

Order.title: Order Object

OrderCosts.description: Describes the costs of the order as a whole, whether paid by credits or real currency. Note that only credit/giftCredit elements are only present and other fields (gross, discount, etc) are omitted if paid for via credits. The reverse is also true if paid for via real currency - credits/giftCredit fields will be omitted, while the others will be present.

credits.description: The total credits this order consumed, if paid by credits.

currency.description: The currency this order was priced in.

discount.description: The discount amount for this order overall.

giftCredit.description: TheThe total gift credits this order consumed, if paid by credits.

gross.description: The gross cost of this order, exclusive of tax.

shipping.description: The total tax-exclusive cost of shipping for this order.

shippingTax.description: The total amount of tax applied to shipping.

tax.description: The total amount of tax on this order, exclusive of shipping.

total.description: The total cost of this order.

OrderCosts.title: Order Costs Object

OrderCustomer.description: Details about the organisation or user that placed this order. For API-originating orders, this will be your organisation details.

address2.description: The sub-premises level of the address, where required.

city.description: The suburb/city level of an address.

country.description: The 2-character ISO code for the country relating to this address.

email.description: The contact email address fro the customer.

notes.description: Any additional notes for this order to pass on to the production team.

postcode.description: The postcode for this address. Note that this may be empty for countries that do not utilise postcodes.

purchaseOrderNo.description: A customer supplied purchase order number, if relevant.

region.description: The state/province/region level abbreviation such as NY, QC, QLD for US, Canadian or Australian addresses, or the full region name for other countries. Note that this may be empty for countries which do not utilise the region level for addressing.

OrderCustomer.title: Order Customer Details Object

OrderItem.description: The order item object provides detail on a component of a larger order, along with detail related to add-on components to this item (ie, gift cards, additional envelopes).

artwork.description: The artwork ID relevant to this item, if a printed card/letter.

costs.description: The total cost of this item, whether paid by credits or real currency.

delivery.description: Requested delivery timings and estimated delivery windows for this item.

id.description: Unique identifier for this order item.

label.description: A description of this item, typically the card artwork title.

media.description: The media ID relevant to this item, if a printed card/letter.

quantity.description: The number of units of this item that were ordered.

recipient.description: The recipient's address details for this item.

related.description: A list of related items for this one, such as gift cards and additional envelopes where required.

scheduledDate.description: If requested at order time, the date this item was requested to arrive by.

sender.description: The sender's address details for this item.

shipMethod.description: The shipping method used, one of `standard`, `tracked` or `express`.

shipTo.description: Either `S` for shipping back to the sender, or `D` for shipping direct to the customer.

template.description: The template ID relevant to this item, if a printed card/letter.

timings.description: Lodgement, production and shipping timing information for this item.

tracking.description: Tracking information related to this item, if relevant to the shipping method.

type.description: The type of item this is - typically `card`.

OrderItem.title: Order Item Object

OrderItemAddress.description: Describes an addressing element such as sender or recipient or for a given order item.

address2.description: The sub-premises level of the address, where required.

city.description: The suburb/city level of an address.

company.description: An optional company line, where relevant. May be blank.

country.description: The 2-character ISO code for the country relating to this address.

omitAddress.description: Conditionally present if this address should be omitted from envelopes. Only used for sender addresses.

postcode.description: The postcode for this address. Note that this may be empty for countries that do not utilise postcodes.

region.description: The state/province/region level abbreviation such as NY, QC, QLD for US, Canadian or Australian addresses, or the full region name for other countries. Note that this may be empty for countries which do not utilise the region level for addressing.

OrderItemAddress.title: Order Item Address Object

OrderItemCosts.description: Describes the costs of an individual line item within an order, whether paid by credits or real currency. ApiKeyAuth.description:
The Cardly API uses API keys to authenticate requests. Your API keys can be obtained and managed from your organisation portal.

Each set of API keys provides both test and live mode keys. Test mode keys are prefixed with `test_` and can perform all the functions that live keys can, however they will not perform any mutations. That is, if a test mode key calls the Place Order endpoint, the request will be validated and provide a mostly-identical response as though you'd used a live key, however no actual order will be placed. Test mode responses will always contain a `testMode: true` element as part of the main return body.

Live mode keys are prefixed with `live_` and have none of the restrictions of test mode keys.

Authentication to the API is performed via the `API-Key` header, as per the provided example.

API keys permit many functions to be performed against your organisation, including billable requests. You must keep your keys secure and if you believe them to be compromised, invalidate and re-issue your keys via your organisation portal.

**All API requests must be performed over HTTPS.** Calls made over plain HTTP will be rejected, as will requests without authentication.
ApiKeyAuth.name: API-Key

info.description:
The version 2 Cardly API is organised around REST, with predictable resource-oriented URLs. It accepts JSON-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses and uses standard HTTP response codes and verbs to make understanding and integrating the API as quick and painless as possible.

When you're set up on the Cardly API, you'll be provided with two API keys - one for test mode, the other for live calls. Your test mode key will allow you to make all the calls available in the API, however won't mutate any data. So, you can test your integration and make sure everything works, get back (generally!) the same response as you would for a live call, then switch out your keys when you're ready to move to live ordering.

Currently the API accepts only JSON-encoded bodies for POST requests. As such, please ensure you provide the appropriate `Content-type: text/json` header when forming your requests. Other content types will likely fail as the request body will not be interpreted correctly.

As we release new products and features, the Cardly API will evolve to include access to these where possible. This documentation will also evolve to cover these new features as they're released.

While we do our best to avoid it, in the event we release a breaking change, we'll let you know well in advance so you have time to plan, test and release any updates necessary to accommodate the change.
info.title: Cardly API

Note that you must have sufficient credit on your account to place your order. If you have insufficient credit, a `402` response will be returned with detail on the required credit cost and your current balance.

The `preview` endpoint allows you to generate a quick, low-quality, watermarked preview document for a given piece of card art and template, along with passed user data. You will also be provided with delivery window estimates and a projected credit cost for the order based on your passed data.
